study.trial_registration: clinical research information service (CRIS, https://cris.nih.go.kr/, registration number: KCT0002253 and registration date: 2017.03.07)
study.title: Phantom Acupuncture Induces Placebo Credibility and Vicarious Sensations: A Parallel fMRI Study of Low Back Pain Patients
study.study_design: event-related fMRI experiment; parallel group study
study.randomization: Patients were randomized, i.e., parallel-group study, into real acupuncture (REAL, n=33) and sham control phantom acupuncture (PHNT, n=23) groups.
study.blinding: Patients were told that they would receive real acupuncture treatment during this experiment.
study.population: non-specific low back pain (LBP) patients (right-handed, 25 females, age=38.4±12.7 years old, mean±STD)
study.inclusion_criteria: Patients who reported evoked pain greater than 4 on a 0–10 visual analog scale (VAS) (0: no pain, 10: maximum imaginable pain) when lifting their low back to a height of 4–7 cm in a supine position were included. In addition, patients were screened to confirm their compatibility and safety in an MRI environment.
study.exclusion_criteria: We excluded participants from this study if they: (1) were below 19 years old, (2) had severe pain other than LBP (such as neck pain or headache), (3) had severe radicular pain (pain extended to their lower leg), (4) had neurological or cardiovascular disease, (5) had LBP from an external injury (accident or surgery), or (6) had any possible psychological motivation (compensating accident insurance) that might affect the pain rating.

arms.dropouts: Out of the REAL group, we excluded five LBP patients due to excessive head motion and incomplete data.
After the retrospective reclassification of LBP patients in the PHNT group, four patients were excluded as non-credible.

conditions.dose_or_intensity_label: five acupuncture stimulations per acupoint; each stimulation was 2 sec long; average inter-stimulus interval was 7.9±1.7 sec
five acupuncture stimulations per acupoint; each stimulation was 2 sec long; average inter-stimulus interval was 7.9±1.7 sec
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: The acupuncturist explicitly did not insert or stimulate needles and did not touch any body part of the patient. The patient watched a pre-recorded video clip while the practitioner mimicked stimulation without contact. This constitutes a no-contact phantom acupuncture condition, matching Level 4.

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: four acupoints: bilateral SP13, left SP11, and left ST36
interventions.laterality_exact: bilateral SP13, left SP11, and left ST36
interventions.needle_type_exact: sterilized non-magnetic needles; stainless steel, DongBang Co., Korea
interventions.penetration_exact: Needles were inserted ~2–3 cm deep into four acupoints
interventions.manipulation_exact: manually by ±180° rotation of the needles at ~1Hz during 2-second duration events
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: the acupuncturist manipulated them to induce a specific acupuncture sensation (de-qi) and ensure that the needles were placed correctly
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: a licensed acupuncturist who had more than 10 years of clinical experience and was trained to work in an fMRI experimental environment/protocol
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: Patients lay supine inside the MRI machine, and they were told that they would receive real acupuncture treatment during this experiment.

interventions.penetration_exact: The acupuncturist neither inserted nor stimulated the needles.
interventions.manipulation_exact: The acupuncturist only approached the acupoints with his hand and mimicked the stimulation without touching any body part of the patients, following the auditory cues for stimulation in the same sequence as in the REAL protocol.
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: a licensed acupuncturist who had more than 10 years of clinical experience and was trained to work in an fMRI experimental environment/protocol
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: Patients lay supine inside the MRI machine, and they were told that they would receive real acupuncture treatment during this experiment.

sham_details.sham_device_exact: video clip, which was recorded previously from the REAL group, was carefully chosen to match the body shape and skin appearance of each patient and displayed to the patient
sham_details.sham_penetration_exact: neither inserted nor stimulated the needles
sham_details.sham_location_exact: approached the acupoints with his hand and mimicked the stimulation without touching any body part of the patients
sham_details.sham_manipulation_exact: mimicked the stimulation without touching any body part of the patients
sham_details.sham_credibility_procedure_exact: preparatory procedure was performed, turning on the camera and building the video–body link; displayed video clip to create an illusion of needle insertion and stimulation (i.e., needling credibility)
